newsitem.title: FRANCE: PSA boss wistful about unlikely US project.
newsitem.headline: PSA boss wistful about unlikely US project.

text.p: PSA Peugeot Citroen Chairman Jacques Calvet said on Wednesday the company was unlikely to set up car production in the United States before his scheduled departure next autumn, but he said he would advise his successor to consider such a project.
"I don't think it will happen in my time here but I regret that," he told reporters after a news conference at the Citroen branch's headquarters.
He said he would have liked to see the group, which once exported Peugeot cars to the United States, return to the world's biggest car market, but as a producer.
"It's a source of regret for me not to have had the time, due to other concerns that came up, to set up a project to return to the United States," he said.
Calvet, who is scheduled to retire next fall under the company's bylaws, said he would suggest to his successor to reflect on the possibility.

He had envisaged a project with a partner that would allow the PSA group to produce 60,000 to 80,000 cars annually. He said it would have to be a car targeted specifically to the U.S. market and for U.S. tastes, as he was not a believer in the concept of a "world car" that can be sold anywhere.
"We can't serve the United States with European models or the European market with U.S. models," Calvet said.
